blocks.html: Slips, trips, and falls are among the most common workplace incidents — and most of them are preventable. In the next few minutes you'll learn a simple 3-step response and then make a real decision in a scenario.

items: Recognize common slip, trip, and fall hazards
Apply the 3-step response: secure, report, follow up
Decide what to do when you spot a hazard under pressure

blocks.html: How this works: read each screen, answer the check, then handle a realistic situation. Your choices change what happens next.

options.feedback: Unreported spills cause injuries within minutes. Walking past makes you part of the problem.
options.text: Walk around it — someone else will handle it.

options.feedback: Exactly. Secure first, then report or clean.
options.text: Block the area and report it (or clean it if you're trained and it's safe).

options.feedback: Paper towels hide the hazard without removing it — and nobody knows it's there.
options.text: Cover it with paper towels and leave.

options.feedback: Waiting without blocking the area leaves everyone else exposed in the meantime.
options.text: Stand nearby until the cleaning crew arrives.

blocks.html: When you spot a slip, trip, or fall hazard, run the same three steps every time:

items: 1. Secure the area — block it, warn people, put out a sign. Protect others before anything else.
2. Report or clean — tell your supervisor, or clean it yourself if you're trained and it's safe.
3. Follow up — make sure the root cause (the leak, the cord, the broken tile) actually gets fixed.

choices.feedback: Strong call. You protected people immediately — and by reporting the leak itself, not just the puddle, you made sure it gets fixed instead of happening again tomorrow.
choices.text: Grab two chairs to block the wet area, then call your supervisor about the leak.

choices.feedback: Risky. There's no wet-floor sign, no report, and the cooler keeps leaking — the next person through hits a fresh puddle. Fast isn't the same as fixed.
choices.text: Mop it up quickly yourself and get back to work.

screens.prompt: It's 4:55 PM. Water is spreading from a leaking cooler near the break-room entrance. People are streaming out for the day, most of them looking at their phones. You're the only one who has noticed. What do you do?
screens.title: Decision point: 4:55 PM

screens.failMessage: Review the 3-step response and try again — protecting others starts with securing the area first.
screens.passMessage: You think like a safety owner: secure, report, follow up. That's the habit that prevents injuries.
screens.title: Your results
